A nilpotent version of the first Kac conjecture

Lydia Gösmann
Abstract

We derive a formula for the nilpotent Kac polynomial and define an explicit generalized Kac-Moody Lie algebra (by generators and relations) and conjecture that its graded dimensions recover the constant terms of the nilpotent Kac polynomial. We outline empirical evidence supporting the conjecture and prove it for two special classes of quivers: quivers without oriented cycles except loops and quivers with ”negative enough” Euler form.

1 Introduction

For a dimension vector 𝐝\mathbf{d} of a quiver QQ let A𝐝A_{\mathbf{d}} be the Kac polynomial attached to Q and 𝐝\mathbf{d}. For a finite field 𝔽q\mathbb{F}_{q} the integer A𝐝​(q)A_{\mathbf{d}}(q) is equal to the number A𝐝​(𝔽q)A_{\mathbf{d}}(\mathbb{F}_{q}) of isomorphism classes of absolutely indecomposable representations of QQ of dimension vector 𝐝\mathbf{d} over 𝔽q\mathbb{F}_{q}. The polynomial A𝐝​(t)∈ℤ​[t]A_{\mathbf{d}}(t)\in\mathbb{Z}[t] is monic and of degree 1−⟨𝐝,𝐝⟩1-\langle\mathbf{d},\mathbf{d}\rangle and has nonnegative coefficients.
Furthermore, one can also ask for the number of absolutely indecomposable nilpotent representations. This question is addressed in work of Bozec-Schiffmann-Vasserot [2]. There they developed a formula for the nilpotent and 1-nilpotent Kac polynomial counting nilpotent or 1-nilpotent absolutely indecomposable representations, respectively. In particular, they prove that the constant term of the 1-nilpotent Kac polynomial is the dimension of a generalized Kac-Moody algebra in the corresponding degree. The question of a Lie algebra corresponding to the nilpotent Kac polynomial remained open. In this paper we derive an explicit formula for the nilpotent Kac polynomial and propose an explicit presentation (by generators and relations) of a Lie algebra 𝔤Qn​i​l\mathfrak{g}_{Q}^{nil} and conjecture that its graded dimensions recover the constant terms of the nilpotent Kac polynomial. We give computational evidence, prove consistency with the generalized Kac–Moody case as well as the special case of quivers with negative enough Euler form. Moreover, we observe that the generators are governed by the Le Bruyn–Procesi classification of dimension vectors of simple-representation and we interpret the conjecture in the context of BPS theory. A proof of the conjecture will appear in a forthcoming joint paper with L. Hennecart.

Corollary 2.1.

We have

n𝐝(q)=(−1)dim𝐝⋅q∑i(di2)⋅∑𝐝∗(−1)s⋅q−∑k<l⟨𝐝k,𝐝l⟩⋅[𝐝𝐝1,…,𝐝s]q\displaystyle n_{\mathbf{d}}(q)=(-1)^{\dim{\bf d}}\cdot q^{\sum_{i}{d_{i}\choose 2}}\cdot\sum_{{\bf d}^{*}}(-1)^{s}\cdot q^{-\sum_{k<l}\langle{\bf d}^{k},{\bf d}^{l}\rangle}\cdot\left[{{\bf d}\atop{{\bf d}^{1},\ldots,{\bf d}^{s}}}\right]_{q}

In the paper the formula is stated for characteristic 00, but it is still valid as a point counting formula in 𝔽q\mathbb{F}_{q} for the following reason: The assumption of characteristic 00 is necessary in the proof of theorem 2.2 to conclude that the bijection of motives is indeed an isomorphism. Nevertheless, for counting points over a finite field, a bijection between the motives is sufficient, thus the formula above also provides an explicit expression for the counting polynomial. ∎

3 Conjecture: Nilpotent Kac-Moody algebra

Definition 3.1.

For a quiver QQ the (positive part) of the nilpotent Kac-Moody algebra 𝔤Qn​i​l\mathfrak{g}^{nil}_{Q} is given by the following generators:

  • •

    e𝐬ie_{\mathbf{s}_{i}} for 𝐬i∈I\mathbf{s}_{i}\in I, if the vertex ii has no loops, and

  • •

    e𝐝e_{\mathbf{d}} for any dimension vector 𝐝\mathbf{d} such that supp⁡(𝐝)\supp(\mathbf{d}) is a strongly connected subquiver and ⟨𝐝,𝐬i⟩≤0\langle\mathbf{d},\mathbf{s}_{i}\rangle\leq 0 and ⟨𝐬i,𝐝⟩≤0\langle\mathbf{s}_{i},\mathbf{d}\rangle\leq 0 for all 1≤i≤n1\leq i\leq n.

The generators are subject to the following relation:

  • •

    [e𝐟,e𝐠]=0[e_{\mathbf{f}},e_{\mathbf{g}}]=0 for every pair of generators with (𝐟,𝐠)=0(\mathbf{f},\mathbf{g})=0 and

  • •

    (ad⁡e𝐬i)1−(𝐬i,𝐟)​e𝐟=0(\ad e_{\mathbf{s}_{i}})^{1-(\mathbf{s}_{i},\mathbf{f})}e_{\mathbf{f}}=0, for 𝐟≠𝐬i\mathbf{f}\neq\mathbf{s}_{i}, if 𝐬i∈I\mathbf{s}_{i}\in I and the vertex ii has no loops.

Remark 3.2.

The construction above defines (the positive part of) a Borcherds algebra [1]. The size of the corresponding Cartan square matrix is the number of generators of the above construction, that means all dimension vectors satisfying the conditions above, so it is typically infinite. Moreover, the entry c𝐝,𝐞c_{\mathbf{d},\mathbf{e}} is the symmetrized Euler form (𝐝,𝐞)(\mathbf{d},\mathbf{e}). If 𝐝≠𝐞\mathbf{d}\neq\mathbf{e} then c𝐝,𝐞≤0c_{\mathbf{d},\mathbf{e}}\leq 0 and c𝐬i,𝐬i=2c_{\mathbf{s}_{i},\mathbf{s}_{i}}=2, if 𝐬i∈I\mathbf{s}_{i}\in I and the vertex ii has no loops. All other c𝐝,𝐝c_{\mathbf{d},\mathbf{d}} have an value ≤0\leq 0. A direct calculation shows, that the construction of the Borcherds algebra with this Cartan matrix, reconstruct exactly the above relations.

A program in Julia has been developed counting the generators of the nilpotent Kac-Moody algebra in a given degree. Various verifications form the empirical basis of the following conjecture.

Conjecture 3.3.

For any quiver QQ and any dimension vector 𝐝\mathbf{d} we have

dim𝔤Qn​i​l​[𝐝]=A𝐝n​i​l​(0).\displaystyle\dim\mathfrak{g}_{Q}^{nil}[\mathbf{d}]=A^{nil}_{\mathbf{d}}(0)~.

4 Special cases

4.1 Comparison to generalized Kac-Moody algebra

We recall the definition of the generalized Kac-Moody algebra from [2]:

Definition 4.1.

The (positive part) of the generalized Kac-Moody algebra is given by the following generators

  • •

    e𝐬ie_{\mathbf{s}_{i}} for 𝐬i∈I\mathbf{s}_{i}\in I, if the vertex ii has no loops and

  • •

    e𝐤ie_{\mathbf{k}_{i}} for 𝐤i∈Ki\mathbf{k}_{i}\in K_{i},if the vertex ii has at least one loop.

The generators are subject to the following relation:

  • •

    [e𝐟,e𝐠]=0[e_{\mathbf{f}},e_{\mathbf{g}}]=0 for every pair of generators with (𝐟,𝐠)=0(\mathbf{f},\mathbf{g})=0 and

  • •

    (ad⁡e𝐬i)1−(𝐬i,𝐟)​e𝐟=0(\ad e_{\mathbf{s}_{i}})^{1-(\mathbf{s}_{i},\mathbf{f})}e_{\mathbf{f}}=0 for 𝐟≠𝐬i\mathbf{f}\neq\mathbf{s}_{i}, if 𝐬i∈I\mathbf{s}_{i}\in I and the vertex ii has no loops.

Since the notion of 1-nilpotency and nilpotency coincide, if the quiver has no oriented cycles except loops, we have the following propostion as a consistency check.

Proposition 4.2.

The construction from Definition 4.1 and Definition 3.1 coincide if the quiver QQ has no oriented cycles except loops.

Proof.

Both constructions have the generators e𝐬ie_{\mathbf{s}_{i}} for all 𝐬i∈I\mathbf{s}_{i}\in I. Moreover, since QQ has no oriented cycles except loops, supp⁡(𝐝)\supp(\mathbf{d}) is only a strongly connected subquiver, if 𝐝\mathbf{d} has only one nonzero entry. If this entry is at vertex ii and the vertex ii has at least one loop, we have ⟨𝐝,𝐬i⟩≤0\langle\mathbf{d},\mathbf{s}_{i}\rangle\leq 0 and ⟨𝐬i,𝐝⟩≤0\langle\mathbf{s}_{i},\mathbf{d}\rangle\leq 0 for all 𝐬i∈I\mathbf{s}_{i}\in I. If this entry is at vertex jj and vertex jj has no loops, then ⟨𝐝,𝐬j⟩>0\langle\mathbf{d},\mathbf{s}_{j}\rangle>0 and ⟨𝐬j,𝐝⟩>0\langle\mathbf{s}_{j},\mathbf{d}\rangle>0. This shows that 𝔤Qn​i​l\mathfrak{g}_{Q}^{nil} has the same generators as the generalized Kac-Moody algebra 𝔤Q\mathfrak{g}_{Q}, if QQ has no oriented cycles except loops. Since both algebras have also the same relations, they coincide. ∎

4.2 Negative Enough Euler form

There is another special case, where we can prove the conjecture directly. We say a quiver has a negative enough Eulfer form, if ⟨𝐝,𝐞⟩≤0\langle\mathbf{d},\mathbf{e}\rangle\leq 0, with equality only if 𝐝=0\mathbf{d}=0 or 𝐞=0.\mathbf{e}=0. This means that each vertex has at least two loops, and that there is an arrow from ii to jj for every vertices ii and jj. In this situation the construction of the nilpotent Kac-Moody algebra consists of generators for every dimension vector, since every subquiver is strongly connected and the Euler form is always negative for non-zero dimension vectors. Moreover, there are also no relations between the generators. So the dimension of the nilpotent Kac-algebra is given by multidimensional Lyndon words counts as well as the constant term of the nilpotent Kac-polynmial as the following lemma proves.

For Corollary 3.5. in [6] the condition that the Euler form is negative enough is also necessary.

5 Dimension vectors for simple representations

LeBruyn and Procesi [3] have characterized dimension vectors of simple representations with the following theorem and since the above construction bears a close resemblance to their description, it is worth comparing the two in detail.

Theorem 5.1.

𝐝∈ℕn\mathbf{d}\in\mathbb{N}^{n} is the dimension vector of a simple representation of the quiver QQ if and only if

  • •

    𝐝∈I\mathbf{d}\in I and the vertex ii has no loops or

  • •

    supp⁡(𝐝)\supp(\mathbf{d}) is the extended Dynkin diagram A~n−1\tilde{A}_{n-1} and 𝐝|supp(𝐝)=(1,…,1)\mathbf{d}_{|\supp(\mathbf{d})}=(1,...,1) or

  • •

    supp⁡(𝐝)\supp(\mathbf{d}) is a noncyclic strongly connected subquiver and ⟨𝐝,𝐬i⟩≤0\langle\mathbf{d},\mathbf{s}_{i}\rangle\leq 0 and ⟨𝐬i,𝐝⟩≤0\langle\mathbf{s}_{i},\mathbf{d}\rangle\leq 0 for all 1≤i≤n1\leq i\leq n.

Remark 5.2.
  1. 1.

    Noncyclic here means that supp⁡(𝐝)\supp(\mathbf{d}) is not the extended Dynkin diagram A~n−1\tilde{A}_{n-1}, so QQ has at least n+1n+1 arrows and strongly connected means for every two vertices ii and jj there is a directed path from ii to jj and jj to ii.

  2. 2.

    Note that LeBruyn and Procesi [3] omit the dimension vectors 𝐝∈I\mathbf{d}\in I, where ii is a vertex without loop in their theorem, but they are essential to obtain a complete list of all dimension vectors of simple representations. Moreover, LeBruyn and Procesi use the notation of A~n\tilde{A}_{n} for the extended Dynkin diagram with nn vertices. This has been exchanged to A~n−1\tilde{A}_{n-1} to align with the standard notation of extended Dynkin diagrams.

Definition 5.3.

We call the dimension vectors 𝐝\mathbf{d} such that 𝐝∈I\mathbf{d}\in I and the vertex ii has no loops real simples and all the other dimension vectors of a simple representation imaginary simples.

Lemma 5.4.

The dimension vectors given rise to a generator in the construction of the nilpotent Kac-Moody algebra are exactly the real simples and all multiples of the imaginary simples.

Proof.

For a real simple 𝐝\mathbf{d}, e𝐝e_{\mathbf{d}} is a generator of 𝔤Qn​i​l\mathfrak{g}_{Q}^{nil}. Lets assume 𝐝\mathbf{d} is a multiple of a imaginary simple. This means, that either supp⁡(𝐝)\supp(\mathbf{d}) is the extended Dynkin diagram A~m\tilde{A}_{m} for some mm and d|supp(𝐝)=(k,…k)d_{|\supp(\mathbf{d})}=(k,\dots k) for k∈ℕk\in\mathbb{N} or s​u​p​p​(𝐝)supp(\mathbf{d}) is a noncyclic strongly connected subquiver and ⟨𝐝,𝐬i⟩≤0\langle\mathbf{d},\mathbf{s}_{i}\rangle\leq 0 and ⟨𝐬i,𝐝⟩≤0\langle\mathbf{s}_{i},\mathbf{d}\rangle\leq 0 for all si∈Is_{i}\in I. (For a dimension vector 𝐝\mathbf{d} such that supp⁡(𝐝)\supp(\mathbf{d}) is noncyclic strongly connected the same is true for k​𝐝k\mathbf{d} with k∈ℕk\in\mathbb{N}. Furthermore, if ⟨𝐬i,𝐝⟩≤0\langle\mathbf{s}_{i},\mathbf{d}\rangle\leq 0 and ⟨𝐝,𝐬i⟩≤0\langle\mathbf{d},\mathbf{s}_{i}\rangle\leq 0 for all vertices ii, we have ⟨𝐬i,k​𝐝⟩=k⁡⟨𝐬i,𝐝⟩≤0\langle\mathbf{s}_{i},k\mathbf{d}\rangle=k\langle\mathbf{s}_{i},\mathbf{d}\rangle\leq 0 and ⟨k​𝐝,𝐬i⟩=k⁡⟨𝐝,𝐬i⟩≤0\langle k\mathbf{d},\mathbf{s}_{i}\rangle=k\langle\mathbf{d},\mathbf{s}_{i}\rangle\leq 0 for all vertices ii.) If 𝐝\mathbf{d} is of the second form, then e𝐝e_{\mathbf{d}} is obviously a generator of 𝔤Qn​i​l\mathfrak{g}_{Q}^{nil}. Moreover, if 𝐝\mathbf{d} is of the first form we have ⟨si,d⟩=⟨d,si⟩=0\langle s_{i},d\rangle=\langle d,s_{i}\rangle=0, so e𝐝e_{\mathbf{d}} is also a generator of 𝔤Qn​i​l\mathfrak{g}_{Q}^{nil}.
Now we assume that e𝐝e_{\mathbf{d}} is a generator of 𝔤Qn​i​l\mathfrak{g}_{Q}^{nil}, such that 𝐝\mathbf{d} is not a real simple. Then supp⁡(𝐝)\supp(\mathbf{d}) is strongly connected and ⟨𝐝,𝐬i⟩≤0\langle\mathbf{d},\mathbf{s}_{i}\rangle\leq 0 and ⟨𝐬i,𝐝⟩≤0\langle\mathbf{s}_{i},\mathbf{d}\rangle\leq 0 for all 𝐬i∈I\mathbf{s}_{i}\in I. If supp⁡(𝐝)\supp(\mathbf{d}) is moreover also noncyclic strongly connected, then it is an imaginary simple. Otherwise, supp⁡(𝐝)\supp(\mathbf{d}) is the extended Dynkin quiver A~m\tilde{A}_{m} for some mm. For the quiver A~m\tilde{A}_{m} the only dimension vectors 𝐝\mathbf{d} with ⟨si,d⟩≤0\langle s_{i},d\rangle\leq 0 and ⟨d,si⟩≤0\langle d,s_{i}\rangle\leq 0 for all 𝐬i∈I\mathbf{s}_{i}\in I are the ones of the form (k,…,k)(k,\dots,k) for k∈ℕk\in\mathbb{N}, so exactly the multiples of the dimension vectors of a simple representation corresponding to A~n\tilde{A}_{n}. ∎

6 Interpretation in the Context of BPS Theory

The following observations are due to B. Davison and L. Hennecart (private communication):
In their paper [5] Davison, Hennecart and Schlegel Mejia construct in Corollary 1.8. a PBW isomorphism, that relates a certain generalized Kac-Moody Lie algebra 𝔫AB​P​S,𝒮​𝒩,+\mathfrak{n}^{BPS,\mathcal{SN},+}_{A} to the Borel-Moore homology of the stack of seminilpotent representations of the preprojective algebra ΠQ\Pi_{Q}. Since 𝔫AB​P​S,𝒮​𝒩,+\mathfrak{n}^{BPS,\mathcal{SN},+}_{A} is (the positive part of) a generalized Kac-Moody Lie algebra, it is entirely determined by its generators, which are given by the i!i^{!}-restriction of a certain perverse sheaf 𝒢\mathcal{G} for the inclusion i:ℳQ↪ℳΠQi:\mathcal{M}_{Q}\hookrightarrow\mathcal{M}_{\Pi_{Q}} of affine coarse moduli spaces. Using a result of [2] this isomorphism yields that the generating function of the ddth graded part of 𝔫AB​P​S,𝒮​𝒩,+\mathfrak{n}^{BPS,\mathcal{SN},+}_{A} is the nilpotent Kac polynomial Adn​i​l​(Q)A_{d}^{nil}(Q) and the constant term is obtained by restricting to the zeroth cohomology. Altogether, Conjecture 3.3 is equivalent to:

Conjecture 6.1.

The dimension of the derived global sections of H0(ℳQ,i!𝒢𝐝)H^{0}(\mathcal{M}_{Q},i^{!}\mathcal{G}_{\mathbf{d}}) is 11 if 𝐝\mathbf{d} satisfies one of the conditions in Definition 3.1 and 00 otherwise.

Instructions for reporting errors

We are continuing to improve HTML versions of papers, and your feedback helps enhance accessibility and mobile support. To report errors in the HTML that will help us improve conversion and rendering, choose any of the methods listed below:

  • Click the "Report Issue" () button, located in the page header.

Tip: You can select the relevant text first, to include it in your report.

Our team has already identified the following issues. We appreciate your time reviewing and reporting rendering errors we may not have found yet. Your efforts will help us improve the HTML versions for all readers, because disability should not be a barrier to accessing research. Thank you for your continued support in championing open access for all.
